stem: A 62-year-old man with ischaemic cardiomyopathy and an ejection fraction of 30% remains breathless (NYHA class II-III) despite an ACE inhibitor and a beta-blocker at target doses, with potassium 4.4 mmol/L and normal renal function. Which additional class has the best evidence for reducing MORTALITY in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction?
concept: In HFrEF, mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonists (spironolactone/eplerenone) reduce mortality when added to an ACE inhibitor and beta-blocker (RALES/EMPHASIS-HF). Loop diuretics relieve congestion but have no proven mortality benefit; digoxin reduces hospitalisation but not mortality.
reference: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 21e - Heart Failure: Management
subject: Medicine
